titles: A Pomodoro timer that grows a living pond
Focus for 25 minutes. Watch the pond change.
One HTML file, zero dependencies, a tiny ecosystem
post:
I built a small focus timer for people who like seeing progress instead of collecting streak badges.

Eco-Pomodoro is an eco-friendly Pomodoro timer: every completed focus session advances a tiny pond. Plankton multiplies, weeds grow, fish breed and pass on their color, tadpoles become frogs, and koi unlock after 20 hours of real focus time. Breaks slow the ecology down; idle time freezes it.

It is a single index.html with no build step, no account and no network requests. Saves stay in localStorage and can be exported as JSON. Timing uses timestamps rather than frame counts, so switching tabs or refreshing does not drift the countdown.

Try the browser demo: https://timyin7.github.io/Eco-Pomodoro/
Source and setup notes: https://github.com/timyin7/Eco-Pomodoro

I would especially like feedback on whether the pond feedback actually helps you come back for a second session.

claims.statement: The app is a single index.html with no build step and no dependencies; it can be opened offline.
Saves are stored in localStorage, auto-saved every 8 seconds, and can be exported or imported as JSON.
A live browser demo is served at https://timyin7.github.io/Eco-Pomodoro/ and shows the 25:00 timer and pond.
claims.source: assets/demo-screenshot.png captured from the live Pages URL

claims.statement: Timing is based on Date.now() timestamps and eco time uses segmented settlement, with catch-up capped at 30 minutes.
claims.source: README.md#几个关键设计 and README.en.md#key-designs

claims.statement: Getting started takes three steps: open the app, choose a duration, press Start focus.
System notifications require HTTPS or localhost and degrade to in-page toasts under file://.

cards.title: Focus grows a pond
cards.body: Each completed session feeds a tiny ecosystem: plankton, weeds, fish, shrimp, frogs and koi. Twenty hours of real focus unlocks the koi.

cards.title: One file. No account.
cards.body: A single index.html runs offline with no build step. Saves stay in localStorage and can be exported as JSON whenever you want.

cards.title: See the timer at work
cards.body: Live GitHub Pages demo: a 25:00 focus timer beside the pond. Open it in a browser, no install required.

cards.title: Built to survive tabs
cards.body: Timestamp-based timing and segmented eco-time keep sessions accurate after backgrounding or refresh. Away catch-up is capped at 30 minutes.
